library_entry.summary: Saturn in the 5th from the Moon is unfavourable: worry over children, decline of money, a confused mind and quarrels.
common_outcomes: concern for or separation from children
decline of wealth
confused thinking
quarrels
rare_outcomes: loss of children (Phaladeepika) [maraka: may be read as death of a child]

by_area.personality: Confused mind (Phaladeepika 26.22).
by_area.finance: Decline of wealth (Phaladeepika 26.22; Brihat Samhita 104.43).
by_area.relationships: Quarrels (Brihat Samhita 104.43).
by_area.family: Loss of or separation from sons (Phaladeepika 26.22; Brihat Samhita 104.43).

strengtheners: (softening) Saturn exalted or in its own sign while transiting: does no harm (Phaladeepika 26.31)
(softening) aspect of a benefic on transiting Saturn (Phaladeepika 26.30)
(softening) many bindus in Saturn's ashtakavarga for the sign (Phaladeepika 26.41)
(softening) Saturn yogakaraka, lagna lord, Moon-sign lord, exalted or in a trine natally (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan)
(softening) a planet other than the Sun in the 11th from the Moon (vipareeta vedha, Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan)
weakeners_or_cancellations: (intensifying) Saturn debilitated (Aries) or in an enemy's sign (Phaladeepika 26.32)
(intensifying) a Saturn or other malefic dasa running (Kurczak; Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan)
(intensifying) no or few bindus in Saturn's ashtakavarga for the sign (Raman)
library_entry.phases: Saturn gives its transit results mainly in the last part of the sign: the last decanate (last 10 degrees) per Phaladeepika 26.25 and Saravali 53.10, the second half of the sign per Brihat Samhita 104 (verse on half-signs, numbered 48/49).
library_entry.phrasing_guidance: Suggest care with decisions, investments and children's needs; do not predict harm to children.

library_entry.summary: Saturn in the 7th from the Moon is unfavourable: strain or separation in marriage, wearisome travel and anxiety. Some modern authors count it as a kantaka (thorn) transit.
common_outcomes: spouse's difficulties or distance in marriage
tiring travel
worry and fear
rare_outcomes: separation from spouse and children (Brihat Samhita)

by_area.personality: Troubled by fear (Phaladeepika 26.22).
by_area.relationships: The wife suffers (Phaladeepika 26.22); separation from wife (Brihat Samhita 104.44).
by_area.family: Separation from sons (Brihat Samhita 104.44).

strengtheners: (softening) Saturn exalted or in its own sign while transiting: does no harm (Phaladeepika 26.31)
(softening) aspect of a benefic on transiting Saturn (Phaladeepika 26.30)
(softening) many bindus in Saturn's ashtakavarga for the sign (Phaladeepika 26.41)

(intensifying) a Saturn or other malefic dasa running (Kurczak; Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan)
(intensifying) no or few bindus in Saturn's ashtakavarga for the sign (Raman)

library_entry.disagreements: Which houses count as 'kantaka Shani' varies: Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan names the 4th, 7th and 10th; popular usage often reserves the term for the 4th (see sade_sati/kantaka_dhaiya).
library_entry.phrasing_guidance: Suggest extra patience and communication in partnerships and avoiding unnecessary travel; do not predict divorce or harm to a spouse.

weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter debilitated, in an enemy sign or eclipsed (harm intensified)

library_entry.phases: Phaladeepika 26.25: Jupiter (with Venus) gives its transit results mainly while in the middle third (second decanate) of the sign.
library_entry.disagreements: Phaladeepika 26.2 and Brihat Samhita 104.4 give Jupiter's good houses as 2, 5, 7, 9 only, while Phaladeepika 26.7 and Brihat Samhita 104.31 also make the 11th good. The vedha pairs (2-12, 5-4, 7-3, 9-10, 11-8) come from Phaladeepika 26.7; reading the same pairs in reverse for the bad houses is Raman's general extension. Bindu thresholds differ (Raman: above 4 in the planet's own ashtakavarga; above 30 in the sarvashtakavarga).
library_entry.phrasing_guidance: Present this as a year-long background tone, not a fixed outcome, and say that the dasha, vedha and ashtakavarga can change it. For difficult houses frame it as a time to be careful with money, travel, relationships or health; never predict death, imprisonment or illness as certain, and offer the sourced remedies gently.

library_entry.phases: Each sign takes about 2.5 years; the three Sade Sati signs together about 7.5 years. Svoboda: the period starts 'as if a switch' when Saturn enters the sign before the Moon; a brief entry followed by retrogression gives 'advance notice' of effects that begin fully on the final entry. Classical rule: Saturn gives transit results mainly in the last part of a sign (Phaladeepika 26.25; Saravali 53.10).
library_entry.disagreements: Popular accounts call the Dhaiyas less intense than Sade Sati, while Phaladeepika 26.33 groups the 8th with the 12th and 1st as the most dangerous places for Saturn. Modern authors differ on severity. Svoboda says the sade sati 'creates trouble for most everyone' and is gloomier than the Saturn return. Kurczak calls the fear-based framing 'folklore and myth' and now weighs mainly the 2.5 years over the Moon's own sign. Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan lists severe effects but also good events (marriage, a child, promotion, property) and many exceptions. Raman treats a second Sade Sati as only moderately evil. K.N. Rao edited a group-research book titled 'Saadhe Saati: A Balanced View' (via summary: publisher's blurb only). Wikipedia (tertiary) reports a school holding it is less damaging than folk belief, and a variant reckoning of 45 degrees either side of the natal Moon instead of whole signs.
library_entry.phrasing_guidance: Describe a testing period for health, money and close ties that calls for caution, rest, avoiding risk and debt; never predict death or serious illness. Say plainly that Sade Sati and Dhaiya are popular traditions built on older house-by-house transit rules, and that modern authors disagree about how severe they are.

Svoboda: the period starts 'as if a switch' when Saturn enters the sign before the Moon; a brief entry followed by retrogression gives 'advance notice' of effects that begin fully on the final entry. library_entry.disagreements: Svoboda and Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan treat the whole 7.5 years as difficult; Kurczak weighs mainly this 2.5-year phase and calls the fear framing folklore. Svoboda's 'one school' table puts the worst phase in different signs for different Moon signs, so the peak is not always the worst. Wikipedia reports an unsourced claim that Aquarius Moons are unaffected. Modern authors differ on severity. Svoboda says the sade sati 'creates trouble for most everyone' and is gloomier than the Saturn return. Kurczak calls the fear-based framing 'folklore and myth' and now weighs mainly the 2.5 years over the Moon's own sign. Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan lists severe effects but also good events (marriage, a child, promotion, property) and many exceptions. Raman treats a second Sade Sati as only moderately evil. K.N. Rao edited a group-research book titled 'Saadhe Saati: A Balanced View' (via summary: publisher's blurb only). Wikipedia (tertiary) reports a school holding it is less damaging than folk belief, and a variant reckoning of 45 degrees either side of the natal Moon instead of whole signs.
library_entry.phrasing_guidance: Call it the most demanding stretch, a time to slow down, protect health and keep commitments realistic; stress that outcomes depend on the whole chart and dasha and that many people achieve a great deal in it. Never predict death, illness or ruin. Say plainly that Sade Sati and Dhaiya are popular traditions built on older house-by-house transit rules, and that modern authors disagree about how severe they are.

library_entry.summary: Kantaka (or ardhashtama) Dhaiya: Saturn in the 4th sign from the natal Moon, about 2.5 years, the 'small panoti'. The classical texts treat the 4th as bad (loss of domestic happiness, separation from spouse, friends or relatives, loss of wealth); the 'Dhaiya' label is a modern or popular grouping, and authors disagree on which houses count as 'kantaka'.
common_outcomes: unhappiness or upheaval at home
separation from spouse, friends or relatives
money problems
constant worry or suspicion
change of residence
rare_outcomes: loss of wife (Phaladeepika) [maraka: may be read as death of the spouse]
having to leave one's homeland (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan)

by_area.personality: Ever suspicious, no lasting happiness (Brihat Samhita 104.42); fear, humiliation (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan).
by_area.career: Loss of employment or position (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan).
by_area.finance: Loss of wealth (Phaladeepika 26.22; Brihat Samhita 104.42); debts (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan).
by_area.relationships: Loss of or separation from wife and friends (Phaladeepika 26.22; Brihat Samhita 104.42); neglect by spouse (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan).
by_area.family: Loss of relatives (Phaladeepika 26.22); obstacles on the domestic front (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan).

strengtheners: (softening) Saturn yogakaraka (Taurus, Libra lagnas) or lagna lord (Capricorn, Aquarius) or lord of the Moon sign (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan)
(softening) natal Saturn exalted or in a trine (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan); Saturn well placed natally (Kurczak)
(softening) transiting Saturn exalted or in own sign (Phaladeepika 26.31); aspect of a benefic (Phaladeepika 26.30)
(softening) many bindus in Saturn's ashtakavarga for the sign (Phaladeepika 26.41)
weakeners_or_cancellations: (intensifying) transiting Saturn debilitated (Aries) or in an enemy's sign (Phaladeepika 26.32)
(intensifying) Saturn dasha or sub-period running (Kurczak); malefic dasa-bhukti (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan)
(intensifying) Saturn as 7th and 8th lord, Cancer lagna (Kurczak)
library_entry.phases: Each sign takes about 2.5 years; the three Sade Sati signs together about 7.5 years. Svoboda: the period starts 'as if a switch' when Saturn enters the sign before the Moon; a brief entry followed by retrogression gives 'advance notice' of effects that begin fully on the final entry. Classical rule: Saturn gives transit results mainly in the last part of a sign (Phaladeepika 26.25; Saravali 53.10).
library_entry.disagreements: Naming is inconsistent: Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan calls the 4th 'ardhashtama' and uses 'kantaka' for the 4th, 7th and 10th; popular usage (Wikipedia) calls the 4th 'kantaka' and lists the 7th as well. The classical texts give only the plain 4th-house result. Modern authors differ on severity. Svoboda says the sade sati 'creates trouble for most everyone' and is gloomier than the Saturn return. Kurczak calls the fear-based framing 'folklore and myth' and now weighs mainly the 2.5 years over the Moon's own sign. Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan lists severe effects but also good events (marriage, a child, promotion, property) and many exceptions. Raman treats a second Sade Sati as only moderately evil. K.N. Rao edited a group-research book titled 'Saadhe Saati: A Balanced View' (via summary: publisher's blurb only). Wikipedia (tertiary) reports a school holding it is less damaging than folk belief, and a variant reckoning of 45 degrees either side of the natal Moon instead of whole signs.
library_entry.phrasing_guidance: Speak of a period that can unsettle home, property and peace of mind and that rewards patience in close relationships; never predict a spouse's death or forced exile. Say plainly that Sade Sati and Dhaiya are popular traditions built on older house-by-house transit rules, and that modern authors disagree about how severe they are.

library_entry.summary: The rising (first) phase of Sade Sati: Saturn in the 12th sign from the natal Moon (vyaya Shani), about 2.5 years. The classical texts treat this house as bad (fruitless effort, losses, family illness, grief); modern authors describe the start of Saturn's pressure, awareness of losses and of where more responsibility is needed. Sade Sati as a named 7.5-year period is a later popular tradition, not in the classical texts read.
common_outcomes: rising expenses and losses
tiring work with little reward
worry and grief
health concerns for spouse or children
awareness of where life needs more responsibility
rare_outcomes: theft or loss through enemies (Phaladeepika)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life] for Saturn in the 12th from the Moon (Phaladeepika 26.33)

by_area.personality: Grief and worry (Brihat Samhita 104.45); modern: awareness begins, doubts surface (Kurczak).
by_area.career: Wearisome, unproductive work (Phaladeepika 26.23); loss of position among the dangers of the 12th (Phaladeepika 26.33).
by_area.finance: Money lost to enemies or thieves (Phaladeepika 26.23); unnecessary expenditure (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan, general Sade Sati list).
by_area.relationships: Trouble from enemies (Phaladeepika 26.23).
by_area.family: Illness of wife and sons (Phaladeepika 26.23).
by_area.spirituality: Modern: a time of reflection on losses and responsibilities (Kurczak).

library_entry.phases: Each sign takes about 2.5 years; the three Sade Sati signs together about 7.5 years. Svoboda: the period starts 'as if a switch' when Saturn enters the sign before the Moon; a brief entry followed by retrogression gives 'advance notice' of effects that begin fully on the final entry. Classical rule: Saturn gives transit results mainly in the last part of a sign (Phaladeepika 26.25; Saravali 53.10).
library_entry.disagreements: Kurczak regards the 12th-sign phase as a lead-in and weighs mainly the Moon-sign phase; Svoboda and Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan count the full 7.5 years from entry into the 12th. Modern authors differ on severity. Svoboda says the sade sati 'creates trouble for most everyone' and is gloomier than the Saturn return. Kurczak calls the fear-based framing 'folklore and myth' and now weighs mainly the 2.5 years over the Moon's own sign. Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan lists severe effects but also good events (marriage, a child, promotion, property) and many exceptions. Raman treats a second Sade Sati as only moderately evil. K.N. Rao edited a group-research book titled 'Saadhe Saati: A Balanced View' (via summary: publisher's blurb only). Wikipedia (tertiary) reports a school holding it is less damaging than folk belief, and a variant reckoning of 45 degrees either side of the natal Moon instead of whole signs.
library_entry.phrasing_guidance: Describe the start of a long, slow cycle that rewards simplifying, saving and rest; avoid the word 'curse', do not predict losses as certain, and mention that most people go through two or three Sade Satis. Say plainly that Sade Sati and Dhaiya are popular traditions built on older house-by-house transit rules, and that modern authors disagree about how severe they are.

library_entry.summary: The peak (second) phase of Sade Sati: Saturn over the natal Moon's own sign (janma Shani), about 2.5 years, usually called the most intense. The classical texts treat Saturn here as very bad (illness, losses, separation, humiliation, a bereavement); modern authors describe it as the phase where pressure and grief are processed and character is tested.

separation from family or living away from home
humiliation or loss of recognition
rare_outcomes: danger from poison or fire, confinement (Brihat Samhita)
a bereavement requiring the native to perform funeral rites [maraka: text predicts death of a relative] (Phaladeepika 26.22)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life] (Phaladeepika 26.33)

library_entry.summary: The peak (second) phase of Sade Sati: Saturn over the natal Moon's own sign (janma Shani), about 2.5 years, usually called the most intense. The classical texts treat Saturn here as very bad (illness, losses, separation, humiliation, a bereavement); modern authors describe it as the phase where pressure and grief are processed and character is tested.

illness or low vitality
losses of money or position
separation from family or living away from home
humiliation or loss of recognition
rare_outcomes: danger from poison or fire, confinement (Brihat Samhita)
a bereavement requiring the native to perform funeral rites [maraka: text predicts death of a relative] (Phaladeepika 26.22)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life] (Phaladeepika 26.33)

library_entry.phases: Each sign takes about 2.5 years; the three Sade Sati signs together about 7.5 years. Svoboda: the period starts 'as if a switch' when Saturn enters the sign before the Moon; a brief entry followed by retrogression gives 'advance notice' of effects that begin fully on the final entry. Classical rule: Saturn gives transit results mainly in the last part of a sign (Phaladeepika 26.25; Saravali 53.10).
library_entry.disagreements: Svoboda and Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan treat the whole 7.5 years as difficult; Kurczak weighs mainly this 2.5-year phase and calls the fear framing folklore. Svoboda's 'one school' table puts the worst phase in different signs for different Moon signs, so the peak is not always the worst. Wikipedia reports an unsourced claim that Aquarius Moons are unaffected. Modern authors differ on severity. Svoboda says the sade sati 'creates trouble for most everyone' and is gloomier than the Saturn return. Kurczak calls the fear-based framing 'folklore and myth' and now weighs mainly the 2.5 years over the Moon's own sign. Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan lists severe effects but also good events (marriage, a child, promotion, property) and many exceptions. Raman treats a second Sade Sati as only moderately evil. K.N. Rao edited a group-research book titled 'Saadhe Saati: A Balanced View' (via summary: publisher's blurb only). Wikipedia (tertiary) reports a school holding it is less damaging than folk belief, and a variant reckoning of 45 degrees either side of the natal Moon instead of whole signs.
library_entry.phrasing_guidance: Call it the most demanding stretch, a time to slow down, protect health and keep commitments realistic; stress that outcomes depend on the whole chart and dasha and that many people achieve a great deal in it. Never predict death, illness or ruin. Say plainly that Sade Sati and Dhaiya are popular traditions built on older house-by-house transit rules, and that modern authors disagree about how severe they are.

library_entry.summary: Kantaka (or ardhashtama) Dhaiya: Saturn in the 4th sign from the natal Moon, about 2.5 years, the 'small panoti'. The classical texts treat the 4th as bad (loss of domestic happiness, separation from spouse, friends or relatives, loss of wealth); the 'Dhaiya' label is a modern or popular grouping, and authors disagree on which houses count as 'kantaka'.
common_outcomes: unhappiness or upheaval at home
separation from spouse, friends or relatives
money problems
constant worry or suspicion
change of residence
rare_outcomes: loss of wife (Phaladeepika) [maraka: may be read as death of the spouse]
having to leave one's homeland (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan)

by_area.personality: Ever suspicious, no lasting happiness (Brihat Samhita 104.42); fear, humiliation (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan).
by_area.career: Loss of employment or position (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan).
by_area.finance: Loss of wealth (Phaladeepika 26.22; Brihat Samhita 104.42); debts (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan).
by_area.relationships: Loss of or separation from wife and friends (Phaladeepika 26.22; Brihat Samhita 104.42); neglect by spouse (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan).
by_area.family: Loss of relatives (Phaladeepika 26.22); obstacles on the domestic front (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan).

strengtheners: (softening) Saturn yogakaraka (Taurus, Libra lagnas) or lagna lord (Capricorn, Aquarius) or lord of the Moon sign (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan)
(softening) natal Saturn exalted or in a trine (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan); Saturn well placed natally (Kurczak)
(softening) transiting Saturn exalted or in own sign (Phaladeepika 26.31); aspect of a benefic (Phaladeepika 26.30)
(softening) many bindus in Saturn's ashtakavarga for the sign (Phaladeepika 26.41)
weakeners_or_cancellations: (intensifying) transiting Saturn debilitated (Aries) or in an enemy's sign (Phaladeepika 26.32)
(intensifying) Saturn dasha or sub-period running (Kurczak); malefic dasa-bhukti (Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan)
(intensifying) Saturn as 7th and 8th lord, Cancer lagna (Kurczak)
library_entry.phases: Each sign takes about 2.5 years; the three Sade Sati signs together about 7.5 years. Svoboda: the period starts 'as if a switch' when Saturn enters the sign before the Moon; a brief entry followed by retrogression gives 'advance notice' of effects that begin fully on the final entry. Classical rule: Saturn gives transit results mainly in the last part of a sign (Phaladeepika 26.25; Saravali 53.10).
library_entry.disagreements: Naming is inconsistent: Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan calls the 4th 'ardhashtama' and uses 'kantaka' for the 4th, 7th and 10th; popular usage (Wikipedia) calls the 4th 'kantaka' and lists the 7th as well. The classical texts give only the plain 4th-house result. Modern authors differ on severity. Svoboda says the sade sati 'creates trouble for most everyone' and is gloomier than the Saturn return. Kurczak calls the fear-based framing 'folklore and myth' and now weighs mainly the 2.5 years over the Moon's own sign. Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan lists severe effects but also good events (marriage, a child, promotion, property) and many exceptions. Raman treats a second Sade Sati as only moderately evil. K.N. Rao edited a group-research book titled 'Saadhe Saati: A Balanced View' (via summary: publisher's blurb only). Wikipedia (tertiary) reports a school holding it is less damaging than folk belief, and a variant reckoning of 45 degrees either side of the natal Moon instead of whole signs.
library_entry.phrasing_guidance: Speak of a period that can unsettle home, property and peace of mind and that rewards patience in close relationships; never predict a spouse's death or forced exile. Say plainly that Sade Sati and Dhaiya are popular traditions built on older house-by-house transit rules, and that modern authors disagree about how severe they are.

library_entry.summary: Siddha, Venus's seven-year yogini, is the 'accomplishment' period: success in undertakings, wealth, comforts, honour, romance and family celebrations such as children's marriages.
common_outcomes: success in what one undertakes
wealth, jewellery, comforts, good housing
honour and power from authority
romance and pleasures
marriages and celebrations in the family
rare_outcomes: gains from speculation and shares (Chugh)

by_area.personality: Confident and accomplished.
by_area.career: Success in undertakings; authority and favour from rulers; career betterment.
by_area.finance: Much wealth, ornaments, trade gains, speculation gains (Chugh).
by_area.relationships: Romance; good company.
by_area.family: Marriages of children and celebrations.
by_area.spirituality: Sattvic dharma and true knowledge (Mansagari).

strengtheners: Venus exalted, in moolatrikona, own or friendly sign (Mansagari)
Venus well placed and unafflicted (Chugh)
sub-period of a benefic yogini (Chugh: benefic-benefic very good)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus combust, debilitated or in an enemy sign (Mansagari: period becomes middling)
Venus weak or afflicted (Chugh)
sub-period of a malefic yogini (Chugh: benefic main with malefic sub = bad tending to neutral)
library_entry.disagreements: Mapping: BPHS 46.197-198 and the main Mansagari verse give Venus for Siddha; a variant cited in Mansagari ('of some') swaps Dhanya to Mercury and Bhadrika to Jupiter, and assigns Ketu at the end of Sankata (Jhanji: some give Sankata's first half to Rahu and second half to Ketu). Durations 1-8 years (36 total) agree across BPHS 46.200, Mansagari v.5 and all modern sources. Kursija's English for Pingala says 'free from' the diseases, contradicting the Mansagari Sanskrit and Hindi. Chugh lets the planet's placement modify results; Kursija says predict by natural results only.
library_entry.phrasing_guidance: Describe the yogini as the tone of a period of 7 years and always say the planet's condition and the running Vimshottari dasha shape how it shows. Keep it encouraging without promising specific gains.

library_entry.summary: Sankata, Rahu's eight-year yogini, is the 'crisis' period: losses, illness and weakness, fear of fire and enemies, separations, legal or official trouble and confusion; the texts tie the gravest dangers to it.
common_outcomes: losses and setbacks; loss of position
illness and physical weakness
separation from spouse or children
fear of enemies; legal or official trouble
confusion or delusion
rare_outcomes: fire danger to home or property (Mansagari, Kursija)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death]: Mansagari says death occurs only in a Sankata dasha or antardasha

by_area.personality: Confusion and delusion; dejection.
by_area.career: Loss of position; dishonour; legal cases (Chugh).
by_area.finance: Losses.
by_area.health: Disease, wasting, weakness; loss of virility (Kursija).
by_area.relationships: Fear of enemies.
by_area.family: Separation from spouse and children; distress to the relative signified by Rahu's house (Chugh).

strengtheners: Rahu exalted, in moolatrikona, own or friendly sign (Mansagari)
Rahu well placed and unafflicted (Chugh)
sub-period of a benefic yogini (Chugh: benefic-benefic very good; malefic main with benefic sub = good tending to neutral)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Rahu combust, debilitated or in an enemy sign (Mansagari: period becomes middling)
Rahu weak or afflicted (Chugh)
sub-period of a malefic yogini (Chugh: malefic-malefic very bad)
library_entry.phases: Mansagari (variant, vv.3-4): Ketu is assigned to the end of Sankata; Jhanji: some give the first half to Rahu and the second half to Ketu.
library_entry.disagreements: Mapping: BPHS 46.197-198 and the main Mansagari verse give Rahu for Sankata; a variant cited in Mansagari ('of some') swaps Dhanya to Mercury and Bhadrika to Jupiter, and assigns Ketu at the end of Sankata (Jhanji: some give Sankata's first half to Rahu and second half to Ketu). Durations 1-8 years (36 total) agree across BPHS 46.200, Mansagari v.5 and all modern sources. Kursija's English for Pingala says 'free from' the diseases, contradicting the Mansagari Sanskrit and Hindi. Chugh lets the planet's placement modify results; Kursija says predict by natural results only.
library_entry.phrasing_guidance: Describe the yogini as the tone of a period of 8 years and always say the planet's condition and the running Vimshottari dasha shape how it shows. Frame difficulties as a period calling for patience and care; never predict death, imprisonment, disability or the death of relatives, and mention remedies gently.

windows.method: A house is double-transited while Jupiter and Saturn each occupy it or aspect it (Jupiter 5/7/9, Saturn 3/7/10), counted from the lagna; see dasha_principle/transits_during_dasha.

Sun.summary: The Darakaraka is the planet with the lowest degree in its sign and signifies the spouse; the planet itself (not the 7th from it) describes the partner.
Sun.significations: wife or husband (Jaimini 1.1.18; BPHS 32.13-17 'Streekaraka'; Raman art. 14)

Moon.summary: The Putrakaraka is the fifth planet by degree in the 7-karaka scheme (sixth in the 8-karaka) and signifies children; with the Atmakaraka it forms a key raja yoga.
Moon.significations: children (Jaimini 1.1.16; BPHS 32.13-17; Raman art. 12); subordinates and followers (PVR 8.2 note)

Mars.summary: The Matrikaraka is the fourth-highest planet by degree and signifies the mother; in the 7-karaka tradition it may also stand for children.
Mars.significations: the mother (Jaimini 1.1.14 Abhyankar / 1.1.15 B.S. Rao; BPHS 32.13-17; Raman art. 11); children as well, for those who merge the mother and son karakas (Jaimini 1.1.19; BPHS 32.13-17)

Mercury.summary: The Atmakaraka is the planet with the highest degree within its sign; it stands for the self or soul and is the 'king' of the chart, whose condition colours the whole horoscope and governs bondage and liberation.
Mercury.significations: the native's self and soul (Jaimini 1.1.10-11 Abhyankar numbering; BPHS 32.3-8); bondage and release - misery and happiness (Jaimini 1.1.11 Abhyankar / 1.1.12 B.S. Rao); the main reference point for the karakamsa (its navamsa sign) and for raja yogas, sustenance and spiritual progress

Jupiter.summary: The Gnatikaraka is the sixth planet by degree in the 7-karaka scheme (seventh in the 8-karaka) and signifies cousins and kinsfolk; it is widely used for rivals and obstacles.
Jupiter.significations: kinsfolk and cousins (Jaimini 1.1.17; B.S. Rao; Raman art. 13); rivals and enemies in common use; literal meaning paternal cousin (PVR 8.2 note)

Venus.summary: The Amatyakaraka is the planet with the second-highest degree; as the 'minister' to the Atmakaraka it shows counsel, career and the means by which the native rises.
Venus.significations: ministers and advisers (Jaimini 1.1.12 Abhyankar / 1.1.13 B.S. Rao; PVR 8.2); profession (P.S. Sastri on Uttara Kalamrita ch. 4); career elevation and social status (Murthy ch. 10)

Saturn.summary: The Bhratrikaraka is the third-highest planet by degree and signifies brothers and sisters; some read it also for courage and manliness.
Saturn.significations: brothers and sisters (Jaimini 1.1.13 Abhyankar / 1.1.14 B.S. Rao; Raman art. 10; PVR 8.2); valour and manliness (P.S. Sastri on Uttara Kalamrita ch. 4)

_karakamsha.summary: With the Atmakaraka in Pisces navamsa, Parasara and Jaimini point to steady righteousness and the aim of final liberation (moksha).

library.summary: Mahapurusha yoga of Venus: Venus in its own sign (Taurus, Libra) or exaltation (Pisces) in a kendra. It marks comfort, wealth, vehicles, beauty, artistic taste and a happy married and family life.
library.rarity_and_weight: Possible for every lagna in some kendra (Raman's table). Raman: unblemished cases exceptional; in most charts of limited political value. Frawley: these yogas are not uncommon.
library.timing: Venus's dasa and bhuktis (Saravali 38.22; Raman introduction; Jataka Parijata 7.66). Rath times it through the dasa of the sign containing the yoga (Narayana/sign dasa usage).
library.phrasing_guidance: Present as comfort, taste, charm and a good domestic life, scaled by Venus's strength; do not imply indulgence or infidelity as fixed traits; omit lifespans.

library.summary: A link (conjunction, exchange, mutual aspect, or one placed in the other's kind of house) between the lord of an angle (1, 4, 7, 10) and the lord of a trine (1, 5, 9) is the basic Parashari Raja Yoga for status, power and prosperity. Modern writers stress that some such link exists in many charts, so the result depends on the strength, closeness and freedom from affliction of the two planets.
library.rarity_and_weight: Common. PVR (11.7.2) says the conjunction of a quadrant lord and a trine lord is found in many charts and its magnitude depends on strength and closeness. Raman (HJH) gives it substantial effect only within 12 degrees. In 300 Combinations, Raman says a merely theoretical Raja Yoga is of no consequence. Laghu Parashari and BPHS 41.29-34 grade it by the planets' strength and divisional dignity. Weight: moderate by default; high only when the lords are strong, close, unblemished and involve the 9th/10th lords.
library.timing: Laghu Parashari (Verma sl. 18-19, 34): greatly auspicious results come in the dasa and bhukti of the yogakaraka planets. Related inauspicious planets give mixed results in their bhuktis. Results start in the dasa of one yoga lord and the bhukti of a related planet; if the yoga starts in a maraka's bhukti, it brings recognition more than real gain. Phaladeepika 20.54: in a yogakaraka's dasa, Raja Yoga begins in the bhuktis of the karaka planets and is increased by malefic bhuktis that follow. Raman (300 Combinations, Introduction): the stronger of the two yoga planets fulfils most of the yoga in its own dasa and the weaker as sub-lord. Jataka Parijata 7.66 note: Raja Yogas fructify in the dasa/antardasa of the lord or occupant of the lagna or 10th.
library.phrasing_guidance: Present it as potential for rising responsibility and recognition, not guaranteed power or wealth. Because many charts have some kendra-trikona link, mention it only when the planets are strong and close, and tie it to the dashas of those planets.

library.summary: A yogakaraka is a single planet that rules both an angle and a trine from the lagna. It is a Raja Yoga in itself: Venus for Capricorn and Aquarius, Saturn for Taurus and Libra, Mars for Cancer and Leo. Its strength and placement decide how much status and prosperity its periods bring.
library.rarity_and_weight: Structural: half the lagnas have a single-planet yogakaraka (Cancer, Leo, Taurus, Libra, Capricorn, Aquarius per Raman HJH), so its presence is fixed by the lagna and says nothing by itself. Its weight comes from its strength and placement (Raman HJH; Laghu Parashari).
library.timing: Dasas and bhuktis of the yogakaraka (Laghu Parashari sl. 18). Phaladeepika 20.54 says that within the yogakaraka's dasa, results begin in the bhuktis of the karaka planets. Laghu Parashari sl. 34 says a yogakaraka does not give its yoga results in its own bhukti of its own dasa (Verma's note).
library.phrasing_guidance: Describe the yogakaraka as the chart's most supportive planet, whose periods tend to bring growth and recognition in proportion to its strength. Do not promise wealth or power, and say plainly when the planet is weak or afflicted.

library.summary: Neecha Bhanga means cancellation of debilitation. A debilitated planet is relieved, and in many texts turned into a Raja Yoga, by conditions such as the lord of its sign, or of its exaltation sign, being in a kendra from the lagna or Moon, or the planet being exalted in navamsa or retrograde. Texts and modern writers say a well-cancelled debilitation can give rise from humble beginnings and even outstanding results.
library.rarity_and_weight: Debilitation itself affects many charts, and the kendra-lord conditions are often met, so some cancellation is common. Frawley's two-factor rule and Raman's caution (no. 246) argue for weighting it only when several conditions combine and the planet is otherwise strong. Raman (300 nos. 245-263 remarks) gives true Neechabhanga Raja Yogas the same weight as other Raja Yogas.
library.timing: Rath: the elevation comes suddenly when the debilitated planet is in an exalted navamsa. Rath (Mother Teresa example) times its fame to the Narayana dasa of the relevant sign. In Bhavartha Ratnakara's Capricorn example, Jupiter gives money through brothers (in its period, per Raman's note). Otherwise no specific dasa rule in the sources read.
library.phrasing_guidance: Describe it as a weakness that turns into strength through effort or circumstance, often after an early struggle. Do not promise a sudden rise, and do not label the planet simply 'debilitated' when a cancellation applies.

library.summary: Mercury conjoined with the Sun (Budha-Aditya, also called Nipuna yoga): intelligence, skill in work, reputation and comfort. Because Mercury is never far from the Sun it is very common, and modern writers require Mercury not to be combust for it to count.
library.rarity_and_weight: Very common in the rasi chart because Mercury never strays far from the Sun (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.2); 'not, of course, rare' (Raman no. 24). Raman treats the solar yogas as indicating ego development, not comparable in eminence to raja yogas (no. 18 remarks on the solar yogas).
library.timing: Periods of the Sun, Mercury and the sign holding the conjunction; results also felt throughout life (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.2.4).
library.phrasing_guidance: Present lightly, as a sign of intelligence and practical skill; note it is common. Give it extra weight only when Mercury is clear of combustion or the yoga repeats in D-9/D-10. Do not repeat the 7th-house danger statements.

library.summary: A natural benefic in the 10th house from the lagna or from the Moon (BPHS and Santhanam: only benefics, no malefic there). 'Amala' means spotless: it gives lasting fame, clean character and honour, with wealth according to Phaladeepika.
library.rarity_and_weight: Two reference points make the basic form fairly easy to meet; sources give no frequency figure. Santhanam: a pure Amala yoga gives name and fame for decades. Raman weighs it by the strength of the benefic.
library.timing: Santhanam's example: results (a business start) came in the sub-period of the benefic forming it (Mercury in Venus dasa). Raman: any planet in the 10th from lagna or Moon gives wealth in its dasa.
library.phrasing_guidance: Present as a sign of good reputation and ethical conduct in public life. Do not promise permanent fame; mention that a malefic sharing the 10th weakens it.

library.summary: Sunapha forms when one or more planets other than the Sun occupy the 2nd sign from the Moon. The texts tie it mainly to self-earned wealth, intelligence and standing, coloured by whichever planet forms it.
library.rarity_and_weight: Varahamihira counts 31 combinations of the five planets for Sunapha (Brihat Jataka 13.4; Raman no. 4 remarks); Saravali 13.3 says 30. The yoga is common because any of five planets will do. Raman weighs it by the nature and strength of the occupying planets and says it strongly influences finances (no. 2).
library.timing: Results show in the dasas and bhuktis of the planets that form the yoga (Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2).
library.phrasing_guidance: Present this as a supportive yoga for earning by one's own effort. Name the planet forming it and its condition, since that changes the flavour a lot. Avoid promising wealth or rank; say it supports them when the forming planets are strong.

library.summary: Dhana yogas are links among the wealth houses: the 2nd (wealth), 11th (gains), 5th and 9th (fortune) and the lagna. The classic form joins the 2nd and 11th lords with the 5th and 9th lords. These yogas promise wealth in proportion to the strength of the planets involved.
library.rarity_and_weight: Common in some form. Raman's note to Bhavartha Ratnakara ch. 2 st. 4 says the majority of horoscopes have the weaker form that gives humble wealth. Raman (HJH) warns not to predict wealth unless other strong Dhana yogas exist. The lagna-specific BPHS forms are much rarer and stronger.
library.timing: Dasas of the 5th and 9th lords and planets conjunct them (BPHS 41.16; PVR 11.9). Periods and sub-periods of the 2nd-5th or 2nd-11th exchanging lords, and of the 5th and 9th lords in their own houses (Raman HJH).
library.phrasing_guidance: Speak of capacity to earn and build resources, which shows most in the periods of the lords involved. Never promise riches; Bhavartha Ratnakara itself says most charts get modest rather than great wealth.

library.summary: Parivartana is a mutual exchange of signs: planet A sits in a sign of planet B while B sits in a sign of A. Phaladeepika counts 66 possible exchanges between house lords. It divides them into Maha (28, good houses), Khala (8, involving the 3rd lord) and Dainya (30, involving the 6th, 8th or 12th lords), whose results range from wealth and authority to misfortune.
library.rarity_and_weight: Phaladeepika's count: 28 of the 66 possible exchanges are Maha, 8 Khala and 30 Dainya. Frawley rates exchange among the most powerful connections. Weight depends on the houses involved and the planets' strength (Raman HJH).
library.timing: Raman (HJH) times the 2nd-5th and 2nd-11th exchanges to the periods and sub-periods of those lords. Rath reads results through the exchanged planets' periods and dasas (e.g. Mars-Venus exchange in the D-16, Crux PDF p. 87).
library.phrasing_guidance: Explain an exchange as two areas of life becoming closely tied, each planet acting for the other. Say which kind (Maha, Khala or Dainya) it is from the houses involved. Avoid harsh language for Dainya; say it points to effort and obstacles around the dusthana matters.

library.summary: Shakata (Sakata, 'cart') is the Moon in the 6th, 8th or 12th from Jupiter (equivalently Jupiter in the 12th, 6th or 8th from the Moon). It gives fortune that rises and falls like a cart wheel: luck is lost and regained. Most texts cancel it when the Moon (or Jupiter) is in a kendra from the lagna. A separate Nabhasa Sakata (all planets in the 1st and 7th) shares the name.
library.rarity_and_weight: The Moon-Jupiter form is common, since it needs only a sign relation between two bodies. Raman gives it modest weight: in many charts the poverty was nominal and fortune was only obstructed at times (no. 12). The Nabhasa form, needing all planets in two signs, is rare. Nabhasa yogas act throughout life (BPHS 35.50).
library.timing: Raman, citing a Sukra Nadi: the effects come each time the Moon transits the 6th, 8th or 12th from natal Jupiter (no. 12). Rath: in Jupiter's dasa (Crux ch. XI). Nabhasa form: in all dasas (BPHS 35.50; Brihat Jataka ch. 12 notes).
library.phrasing_guidance: Describe ups and downs in fortune that recover, not lasting poverty. Check the kendra cancellation first, and say which version (Moon-Jupiter or all planets in the 1st and 7th) the calculator found.

library.summary: 'Grahan' (eclipse) yoga, the Sun or the Moon conjoined with Rahu or Ketu, is a later, popular name; the classical texts read here do not define a yoga by that name. They do treat birth at an actual eclipse as inauspicious and needing remedy. They also treat the Moon 'seized' by Rahu or Ketu as spoiling lunar yogas and pointing to poverty when malefics aspect it. Modern authors read the node-luminary conjunction as an eclipse of that light, with obstructed or transformed results.
library.rarity_and_weight: The sign-conjunction form is fairly common. The texts give heavy weight only to an actual eclipse at birth (BPHS ch. 91; Uttara Kalamrita 8.8; Saravali 10.37-38). For the conjunction, Jataka Parijata 7.107 treats it as a modifier that mixes the lunar yogas rather than as a yoga by itself.
library.timing: Rath: in Rahu dasa (renunciation in his ch. XV example; the mother's sudden death in a Rahu dasa in his ch. XII example).
library.phrasing_guidance: Say that this is a modern label, and that a same-sign conjunction is not an actual eclipse at birth. Describe it as pressure or intensity on the Sun's or Moon's matters (vitality, father, mind, mother) that can also turn inward or spiritual. Never repeat the parent-death or infant-death lines to a user.

principles.summary: A dasha lord brings up the affairs of the houses it rules, the house it sits in, the planets it joins and the planets that aspect it. Its own nature as a planet gives the general flavour of the period; its placement and links decide the specific events.
common_outcomes: List the houses the mahadasha lord rules and occupies, plus the planets it is joined with or aspected by; the period mainly activates those houses.
Read the planet's natural significations (e.g. Sun: father, government; Venus: spouse, comforts) as the background colour of the whole period, then narrow them by its houses.
A well-placed lord improves the houses it rules, occupies or aspects during its period; a weak, badly placed lord harms the same houses.
A planet linked to a house lord carries that lord's matters too (e.g. the Sun with the 5th lord can bring a child in the Sun's period).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika assigns to the dasha all results described elsewhere in the text for the planet's placement, aspects, conjunctions and lordships, so any natal combination involving the planet can surface in its period.
strengtheners: Lord placed in a kendra, trikona or the 11th, in own, exalted or friendly sign, or joined with lords of good houses (BPHS 47.7-11; Phaladeepika 20.14).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Lord in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated, in an enemy sign, combust, or joined with malefics or dusthana lords (BPHS 47.12-15; Phaladeepika 20.14-20).
principles.phrasing_guidance: Name the life areas the period highlights (from the houses ruled and occupied) before saying whether it is easy or hard; avoid predicting a single fixed event.
sources: BPHS 47.2 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
BPHS 47.7-11 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
BPHS 48.2-8 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
Phaladeepika 20.1-21 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
Uttara Kalamrita 6.22-23 (tr. S.S. Sareen; printed as 22.5-23.5)
Uttara Kalamrita 8.97 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV rules 5 and 10

principles.summary: Whether a dasha is good or bad depends first on which houses the planet rules for that lagna: lords of the trikonas (1, 5, 9) give good periods, lords of 3, 6 and 11 give troubled ones, kendra lords depend on whether the planet is a natural benefic or malefic, and a planet ruling both a kendra and a trikona is the best of all (yogakaraka).
common_outcomes: Before reading any dasha, classify each planet for the lagna: trikona lord (good), 3/6/11 lord (bad), kendra lord (natural benefics lose goodness, natural malefics lose harm), 2nd/12th lord (neutral, act by association), 8th lord (bad unless it also rules the lagna).
Expect the dashas of trikona lords and of yogakarakas to be the productive periods of life, and the dashas of 3/6/11 and 8th lords to be the testing ones, other factors equal.
When a planet rules two houses, the one holding its moolatrikona sign weighs more; a good lordship can override a weaker bad one (e.g. 9th lordship over 8th).
rare_outcomes: Uttara Kalamrita calls the periods of 2nd, 3rd and 11th lords medium rather than bad.
strengtheners: A trikona lord in a kendra or a kendra lord in a trikona makes its dasha very favourable (BPHS 48.13; Phaladeepika 20.42).
Exchange or conjunction of the 9th and lagna lords, or of the 10th and lagna lords, makes both dashas very good (BPHS 48.14-17).
weakeners_or_cancellations: A kendra or trikona lord that also rules a bad house does not produce raja yoga by mere connection (BPHS 34.15).
Lords of 6, 8 or 12 become favourable in dasha if associated with a trikona lord (BPHS 48.14).
principles.disagreements: Uttara Kalamrita rates 2nd, 3rd and 11th lords' periods as medium, while BPHS 34 and Laghu Parashari treat 3/11 lords as evil and the 2nd lord as neutral. Santhanam's notes soften the 3/6/11 rule when these lords occupy their own signs.
principles.phrasing_guidance: Say 'this period tends to be supportive / demanding for this rising sign' rather than calling a planet good or evil in itself.
sources: BPHS 34.2-7, 34.13-15 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
Laghu Parashari 6-12 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
Phaladeepika 20.41-42, 20.50-51 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
BPHS 48.9-20 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
Uttara Kalamrita 6.22-23 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XVII and ch. XXIV rules 3 and 11
R. Santhanam, notes to BPHS 48 (vol. 2)

principles.summary: The same dasha gives more or less of its promise according to the lord's strength: exalted, moolatrikona, own or friendly sign raise the good results; debilitation, enemy sign or combustion reduce or spoil them. A planet moving toward its exaltation gives a better period than one moving toward its fall.
common_outcomes: Scale the good results of a dasha by the lord's dignity: full when exalted, about three-quarters in moolatrikona, half in own sign, a quarter in a friend's sign, little or none when debilitated (Phaladeepika's scale).
Treat a combust lord like a debilitated one.
A strong lord in a good house gives the full positive results of its houses; the same lord weak and in a dusthana gives their negative side.
Phaladeepika also classifies dashas as descending (falling from exaltation), middling (friend's or exalted sign), ascending (rising from debilitation) and worst (debilitated or enemy sign).
rare_outcomes: Uttara Kalamrita: a planet with more than 10 rupas of shadbala moving toward exaltation gives an exceedingly favourable dasha; under 5 rupas it brings misery.
Raman: planets on a bhava sandhi (house junction) cannot give their full results in their dashas.
strengtheners: Retrograde planets are listed among those that give the good effects (Phaladeepika 20.14).
Benefic aspect on a weak lord brings some relief (BPHS 47.12-15).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Combustion or planetary war ('eclipsed') counts as weakness (Phaladeepika 20.14, 20.30).
Malefic aspect keeps a weak lord's results adverse (BPHS 47.12-15).
principles.phases: Phaladeepika 20.57: a weak planet in an auspicious sign or amsa gives its good effects in the latter half of its dasha.
principles.disagreements: Phaladeepika 20.30 says the dignity scale is reversed for malefics (their harm, not their good, is fullest in debilitation), while BPHS 48.1 says an exalted natural malefic in a good house gives good results.
principles.phrasing_guidance: Speak of 'how fully' a period delivers rather than whether it delivers at all; a weak lord means more effort for the same result.
sources: BPHS 47.3, 47.7-33 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
BPHS 48.1 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
Phaladeepika 20.14, 20.27, 20.30, 20.56-57 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
Uttara Kalamrita 2.21-22 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV (intro and rule 4)

principles.summary: The dasha lord's condition in the navamsa (D9) modifies its period: vargottama or an own/exalted or benefic navamsa improves results, a bad navamsa limits them even when the D1 position looks strong.
common_outcomes: After judging the D1 position, check the lord's navamsa: vargottama or own/exalted navamsa supports the good results.
Do not promise the full results of a strong D1 position if the navamsa position is weak or afflicted.
A weak D1 planet in a good navamsa still gives mixed results, improving in the second half.
strengtheners: Vargottama (Phaladeepika 20.22; Uttara Kalamrita 6.28).
Own or exalted navamsa (BPHS 47.45-48).
Benefic navamsa (BPHS 47.27-32).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Unfavourable navamsa position (Raman, HPA ch. XXIV).
principles.phases: Phaladeepika 20.57: good results come in the latter half when a weak planet sits in an auspicious amsa.
principles.disagreements: Uttara Kalamrita 6.28 makes an exception: when Venus and Saturn are both very strong (exalted, own or vargottama), their mutual periods are bad (see dasha_principle/venus_saturn_mutual_periods).
principles.phrasing_guidance: Present D9 as a refinement ('the deeper strength of the planet'), not as overriding the main chart.
sources: Phaladeepika 20.22, 20.57 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV (intro)

principles.summary: Rahu and Ketu own no houses of their own, so in their dashas they give the results of the house they occupy and of the planets they join (and, per some, the lord of their sign and planets aspecting them). In a kendra or trikona linked with a kendra or trikona lord they act as yogakarakas; in the 8th or 12th, with maraka lords or debilitated, they trouble.
common_outcomes: Judge a node's dasha from: the house it occupies, the planets conjoined with it (taking on their lordships), the lord of its sign and its strength.
Rahu or Ketu in a kendra or trikona connected with a kendra or trikona lord gives a raja-yoga-like period.
A node in the 3rd, 6th or 11th generally gives good results (Santhanam's note); in the 8th or 12th, troubled periods.
A node joined with a maraka planet or sitting in a maraka relationship can act as maraka in its period.
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika: a benefic joined with Rahu causes harm, especially at the end of the dasha.
Phaladeepika: Rahu in Virgo, Pisces or Scorpio gives honour and property in its dasha, which may be lost at the end.
Uttara Kalamrita: nodes in a trikona aspected by or with the 2nd or 7th lord can cause death; in the 2nd or 7th with the 5th or 9th lord they give wealth and long life.
strengtheners: Exaltation (Taurus for Rahu per BPHS 47; Scorpio for Ketu in BPHS and Uttara Kalamrita).
Association or aspect of benefics and placement in a benefic sign (BPHS 47.34-39; Phaladeepika 19.15).
Link with a kendra or trikona lord (BPHS 34.17; Laghu Parashari 36; Phaladeepika 20.53).
weakeners_or_cancellations: 8th or 12th house, malefic or maraka association, debilitation (BPHS 47.40-43).
Association with 6th, 8th or 12th lords (Uttara Kalamrita 6.15-17).
principles.phases: BPHS 47.40-43 (afflicted Rahu): loss of wealth at the start, some relief in the middle, distress at the end. BPHS 47.3-4: node results come in reverse drekkana order because they are always retrograde. Phaladeepika 20.39: harm from a benefic joined with Rahu peaks at the end of the dasha.
principles.disagreements: Own and moolatrikona signs of the nodes differ: BPHS 47 gives Rahu moolatrikona Gemini and own sign Aquarius (others say Virgo); Uttara Kalamrita 6.19-20 gives moolatrikona Gemini and Virgo and own signs Aquarius and Scorpio. Laghu Parashari stresses the house and conjoined planet; Verma adds aspects from practice; Uttara Kalamrita stresses the lord of the occupied house. Santhanam calls 3/6/11 good for nodes, while BPHS 48.18-20 calls planets in 3/6/11 unfavourable. The nakshatra-lord view of node results was not found in the sources read.
principles.phrasing_guidance: Explain that node periods 'borrow' their tone from the house and companions; avoid sensational language about Rahu.
sources: BPHS 34.16-17 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
BPHS 47.34-43 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
Laghu Parashari 13, 36 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
Phaladeepika 19.15-16, 20.39, 20.53 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
Uttara Kalamrita 6.14-21 and 8.82-88 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
BPHS 44.22-24 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
R. Santhanam, notes to BPHS 48.18-20 (vol. 2)
B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV (Rahu's dasa)

principles.summary: An antardasha is judged partly by where its lord sits counted from the mahadasha lord: in a kendra, trikona, 3rd or 11th from it the sub-period cooperates and is good; in the 6th, 8th or 12th from it the sub-period is hostile and troubled. The dasha lord's sign is treated like a temporary lagna.
common_outcomes: Count from the mahadasha lord's sign to the antardasha lord's sign; 6, 8 or 12 marks a strained sub-period even if both planets are otherwise good.
Also check the antardasha lord's own house from the lagna and its dignity; BPHS judges both.
Treat the mahadasha lord's sign as a lagna and read the antardasha lord's placement from it.
strengtheners: Antardasha lord strong and in a kendra, trikona, 3rd or 11th from the dasha lord (BPHS 52-59 throughout).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Antardasha lord weak, or in 6/8/12 from the dasha lord (BPHS 52.13-14, 52.19-20).
principles.phases: BPHS 53.49: even a well-placed Ketu antardasha in the Moon's dasha may bring loss at its end.
principles.disagreements: Uttara Kalamrita counts the 2nd from the dasha lord as very beneficial, while Raman counts a mutual 2/12 placement as unfavourable. Phaladeepika treats every position except 6/8/12 as good.
principles.phrasing_guidance: Describe a 6/8/12 sub-period as a time of friction between the two planets' agendas, not as a disaster.
sources: Phaladeepika 20.29 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
Uttara Kalamrita 6.21-24 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV rules 12 and 14
Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, sec. 8.6.2

principles.summary: A mahadasha lord shows its results mainly in the sub-periods of planets that are related to it (by conjunction, aspect, exchange or mutual kendra/trikona) or that share its functional character; unrelated or opposite-natured sub-lords give reduced or mixed results, and enemies of the dasha lord bring opposition.
common_outcomes: Find which sub-lords are related to the dasha lord; those are the windows in which the dasha's main promise (good or bad) actually shows.
A sub-lord of the same functional type (e.g. both yogakarakas, or both marakas) intensifies the dasha's theme; an opposite type dilutes it.
A sub-lord who is a natural enemy of the dasha lord or of the lagna lord tends to bring rivals and loss of standing.
principles.phrasing_guidance: Frame related sub-periods as 'when this period's main story plays out'.
sources: Laghu Parashari 30-31 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
Phaladeepika 20.28, 20.44 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
Uttara Kalamrita 8.85-86 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV rule 12

principles.summary: The first sub-period of every mahadasha is the lord's own; it does not deliver the full good or bad promise of the dasha, which comes later in related sub-periods. It is judged by the lord's dignity and house, and by maraka lordship.
common_outcomes: Do not predict the peak events of a mahadasha in its opening sub-period; expect a partial or preparatory taste.
Judge the own sub-period by the lord's natal dignity and house: exalted, own, kendra, trikona or 11th good; debilitated or in a bad house adverse; otherwise medium.
rare_outcomes: Uttara Kalamrita 6.24-25: a dasha lord able to give both yoga and death gives the yoga first, in its own bhukti.
Uttara Kalamrita 8.89: in Saturn's dasha its own bhukti gives Mars-like results and Mars's bhukti gives Saturn's own, and the same applies in Mars's dasha.
principles.disagreements: Laghu Parashari and Phaladeepika say the own sub-period does not give the full results, while Uttara Kalamrita 6.24-25 places the yoga first in the lord's own bhukti.
principles.phrasing_guidance: Call it a 'settling-in' phase of the new period.
sources: Laghu Parashari 29 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
Phaladeepika 20.43-44 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
BPHS 52.1-3 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
Uttara Kalamrita 6.24-25, 8.85, 8.89 (tr. S.S. Sareen)

remedies.remedy: Mrityunjaya japa or worship of the Sun (for the Sun's own sub-period when it rules the 2nd or 7th)
remedies.source: BPHS 52.1-3

principles.summary: Raja yoga results come in the dashas and sub-periods of the related kendra and trikona lords (yogakarakas). Within a yogakaraka's dasha, sub-periods of related planets deliver the most; related malefic or maraka sub-lords still deliver some yoga; unrelated benefic sub-lords between yoga sub-periods keep the good going.
common_outcomes: Identify the related kendra-trikona pairs; their mutual dasha/bhukti is the peak of the yoga.

In a yogakaraka's dasha, grade sub-periods: related yogakaraka best, related benefic next, related inauspicious planet less, related maraka least; unrelated benefic mildly good; unrelated malefic mixed.
A raja yoga that begins in a maraka sub-period brings recognition first; the material benefits come in a following related inauspicious sub-period.
rare_outcomes: Uttara Kalamrita 8.82-83: the yoga is destroyed if the 9th lord also rules the 8th or 12th, or if the 9th and 10th lords join the 8th or 12th lords.
strengtheners: Both lords unblemished (not also ruling bad houses) and free of combustion or debilitation (Verma on Laghu Parashari 32).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Kendra or trikona lord also ruling a dusthana or 3/11 reduces the yoga (BPHS 34.15; Laghu Parashari 15, 32).
principles.phases: Verma on Laghu Parashari 33-34: when a planet is both yogakaraka and maraka, yoga results come first in benefic sub-periods and maraka results later; within a maraka sub-period, the start is good and the later part brings the maraka results.
principles.disagreements: Uttara Kalamrita 8.87 says a yogakaraka does good even in an unrelated planet's bhukti, but 6.24-25 says an unrelated yogakaraka bhukti in an inauspicious dasha becomes distressing. Verma notes Susloka Sataka gives related maraka and related inauspicious bhuktis the same yoga strength, unlike Laghu Parashari.
principles.phrasing_guidance: Present yoga periods as windows of opportunity that still need effort; avoid promising status or wealth outright.
sources: Laghu Parashari 18-19, 32-35 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
Phaladeepika 20.42, 20.45-49, 20.54 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
BPHS 34.11-13 (vol. 1) and 48.9-17 (vol. 2) (tr. R. Santhanam)
Uttara Kalamrita 8.86-87 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV rules 11 and 15

principles.summary: In the dasha of a functionally inauspicious planet (8th lord, 3/6/11 lords), even good sub-lords struggle: an unrelated benefic or yogakaraka sub-period turns out badly, a related one gives mixed results, and another malefic sub-period is very hard.
common_outcomes: Do not expect a benefic sub-period to rescue a malefic mahadasha unless the sub-lord is linked to the dasha lord.
Related good sub-lords soften the period into mixed results; unrelated ones are overridden.
Two malefic lords in 6/8/12 from each other make the worst sub-periods.
principles.phrasing_guidance: Describe these as periods needing patience, where help comes mainly through connected people or planets.
sources: Laghu Parashari 37-38 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
Uttara Kalamrita 6.24-25 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
Phaladeepika 20.22 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)

principles.summary: The 2nd and 7th houses are the maraka (death-inflicting) houses. Their lords, malefics placed in them and malefics joined with their lords are marakas, and their periods are the classical windows for danger to life when the lifespan indicated by other methods is ending; otherwise they bring illness and hardship. Saturn linked to marakas becomes the chief maraka.
common_outcomes: Flag dashas and sub-periods of 2nd and 7th lords and of malefics in or with them as periods of health caution; texts tie actual danger to life to the longevity span worked out separately.
In a maraka dasha, a related benefic sub-lord does not bring the worst; an unrelated malefic sub-lord does.
Also note the 2nd lord's period can bring wealth and the 7th lord's marriage when well placed (Santhanam).
rare_outcomes: BPHS 44.15-21: lords of the 2nd and 12th from the Moon sign can act as marakas (if malefic; if benefic, only illness).
Laghu Parashari 24-25: if death does not come in the marakas' periods, it may come in the 12th lord's or other malefics' periods.
weakeners_or_cancellations: A malefic dasha does not kill in a benefic's sub-period even if they are related (BPHS 44.8).
Raman lists planets that do not kill for certain lagnas even with maraka powers (e.g. the Sun for Cancer, Saturn for Leo, Jupiter for Scorpio).
principles.disagreements: Laghu Parashari's commentators differ on which maraka house is stronger: BPHS 44 and one reading make the 2nd stronger, Verma's preferred reading makes the 7th stronger (counted from the 8th).
principles.phrasing_guidance: Never predict death. Rephrase maraka periods as times to look after health and avoid risks, and say lifespan cannot be judged from one factor.
sources: BPHS 44.2-9, 44.15-24 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
Laghu Parashari 23-28, 39 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
Phaladeepika 20.40, 20.50 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
BPHS 48.2-8 and notes (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
Uttara Kalamrita 8.84-85 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XVII

remedies.remedy: Mrityunjaya japa or Shatarudriya recitation and gift of a cow or female buffalo (Venus as 2nd or 7th lord)
remedies.source: BPHS 47 (Venus dasha, tr. Santhanam, verses 88-89)

remedies.remedy: Gift of a white cow and female buffalo (Moon as maraka in the Sun's dasha)

principles.summary: Venus and Saturn give each other's results in their mutual periods: in Venus dasha and Saturn sub-period Saturn's results come, and the reverse. If both are very strong, their mutual periods can bring a sharp fall; if one is strong and one weak, the strong one gives good results.
common_outcomes: In Venus-Saturn or Saturn-Venus periods, read the sub-lord's promise rather than the dasha lord's.
Be cautious when both Venus and Saturn are exalted, in own sign or vargottama: the classics predict reversal of fortune in their mutual periods.
If both are weak and in 6/8/12 from each other, the texts paradoxically predict good results.
rare_outcomes: Uttara Kalamrita gives similar pair rules for Jupiter-Venus, Saturn-Sun, Mars-Jupiter and Jupiter-Mercury mutual periods when strong and well placed.
principles.phrasing_guidance: Present as a special classical rule to watch, not a certainty of loss.
sources: Laghu Parashari 40 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
Uttara Kalamrita 6.26-32 (tr. S.S. Sareen)

principles.summary: When a planet's results arrive inside its dasha depends on its decanate (drekkana): first decanate at the start, second in the middle, third at the end; a retrograde planet, and always Rahu and Ketu, give them in reverse order.
common_outcomes: Use the lord's drekkana (0-10, 10-20, 20-30 degrees of the sign) to place its main effects in the first, middle or last third of the period, reversed if retrograde or a node.
Weak planets in good signs or amsas improve in the second half (Phaladeepika).
Some planets' periods carry specific end-of-period warnings (Mars, afflicted Rahu, Rahu with a benefic).
rare_outcomes: BPHS 47.27-32: even a strong Mars dasha may bring some unfavourable effects at the end.
principles.phases: Drekkana 1 = start, 2 = middle, 3 = end; reversed for retrograde planets and the nodes (BPHS 47.3-4). Weak planets in good amsas improve in the latter half (Phaladeepika 20.57).
principles.phrasing_guidance: Give phases as tendencies ('more likely early in the period'), not dates.
sources: BPHS 47.3-4 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
BPHS 47.27-32, 47.40-43 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
Phaladeepika 19.16, 20.39, 20.57 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)

principles.summary: Transits time and modify what the dasha promises. The dasha lord's position in the sky when the dasha begins, and its later transits through good or bad houses and signs, raise or lower the results; the Moon's transit relative to the dasha lord does the same day to day. Modern practice (K.N. Rao) times major events by the Jupiter-Saturn double transit within a supporting dasha.
common_outcomes: Check where the dasha lord is transiting when its dasha starts: in the lagna, its exaltation, own or friend's sign is good; in 6, 8 or 12, debilitation or enemy sign is bad. Combine this with the natal position.
Within a dasha, the lord's transit through its own, exalted or friendly sign boosts its houses; transit through debilitation or enemy sign hurts them.
Use transits to time events the dasha already indicates, not to create events the dasha does not support.
For major events, look for Jupiter and Saturn both influencing the relevant house by transit while a related dasha runs.
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika: an auspicious bhukti gives results when the Sun transits the bhukti lord's exaltation sign; an inauspicious one when the Sun passes its debilitation or enemy sign.
strengtheners: Dasha lord transiting the lagna or the 3rd, 6th, 10th or 11th from it (Phaladeepika 20.59).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Natally weak dasha lord transiting anywhere spoils the bhava it signifies (Phaladeepika 20.35).
principles.phrasing_guidance: Present transits as timing triggers inside a period; avoid exact-date promises.
sources: BPHS 47.5-6 and 48.8 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
Phaladeepika 20.34-38, 20.59-61 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV rule 6
Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, p. 53 (dasha-start charts)
K.N. Rao, Ups and Downs in Career (via summary: publisher's description and preface excerpt)
Light on Vedic Astrology blog on K.N. Rao's double transit (via summary)

principles.summary: A yoga in the birth chart gives its results mainly in the dashas and sub-periods of the planets that form it; Nabhasa yogas are an exception, felt throughout life.
common_outcomes: For each major yoga, note the planets forming it and expect its results when their dashas or sub-periods run.
If none of a yoga's planets rules a dasha during the useful years of life, its results stay limited.
Treat Nabhasa (pattern) yogas as lifelong background rather than period-specific.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Uttara Kalamrita 8.98 notes yogas are also influenced by other forces.
principles.phrasing_guidance: Link yoga promises to their periods so the reader sees when potential is most likely to show.
sources: Uttara Kalamrita 8.98 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
BPHS 33.94-99, 35.50 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
Laghu Parashari 18 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)

principles.summary: In the dasha of a malefic, sub-periods of the lords of the 3rd, 5th and 7th nakshatras from the birth star (Vipat, Pratyak, Vadha) bring trouble; the same stars' dashas are classical danger windows for short, medium and long life.
common_outcomes: Count from the birth nakshatra: the lords of the 3rd, 5th and 7th stars are the trouble sub-lords inside a malefic's dasha.
Expect setbacks from rivals, theft or misfortune in those sub-periods.
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika adds the bhukti of the Moon-sign lord or the 8th lord from it in a malefic dasha.
principles.phrasing_guidance: Describe as periods for extra caution; never predict death.

principles.summary: Certain dashas are flagged as difficult by their position in the native's sequence of dashas: Saturn as the 4th dasha, Jupiter as the 6th, and Mars or Rahu as the 5th. A planet at the very end of a sign also gives a dangerous dasha.
common_outcomes: Number the dashas from the one running at birth; if Saturn's is the 4th, Jupiter's the 6th, or Mars's or Rahu's the 5th, read that period cautiously.
principles.phrasing_guidance: Mention only as a supplementary caution, never as the main judgement of a period.

library_entry.summary: Mercury's 17-year mahadasha is described in every source as a period of learning, speech, trade, friends and family happiness, with honour from rulers or superiors when Mercury is strong. When Mercury is joined with malefics, debilitated, combust or in the 6th, 8th or 12th, the same period brings quarrels with relatives, losses, nervous or wind ailments and trouble from authorities. BPHS adds that the start is good, the middle brings recognition and the last part is troubled.
common_outcomes: gain of wealth, reputation and knowledge, royal favour, auspicious functions, happiness from wife and children, profit in business, when Mercury is well placed (BPHS 47.62-65)
meeting friends, personal comforts, fame through the praise of learned people, favour from elders, skill in speech, doing good to others, an elevated position (Phaladeepika 19.10)
money through seniors, relatives and friends, fame and happiness, going on an embassy or errand, income from dealing in gold, some wind ailment (Jataka Parijata 18.133)
garments, large wealth, grain, position, a mansion, fulfilment of wishes when Mercury is auspicious (Uttara Kalamrita, 'Dasas and their effects' sl. 8-9)
rare_outcomes: gain of new lands, cows and horses; money through Brahmins; worship of great men and gods; illness from wind, heat and phlegm (Phaladeepika 19.24, a second verse on Mercury's dasa)
journey to a foreign country and dependence on others when Mercury is with malefics (BPHS 47.66)
loss of wealth through lascivious habits, rheumatism and jaundice when Mercury is in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.67-68)
book writing and fame as a communicator when Mercury is linked to the houses of writing and fame (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, example 52)

by_area.personality: Clear speech, cleverness and a helpful nature (Phaladeepika 19.10); growth of intelligence (BPHS 47.63). When Mercury is afflicted: short temper and weakened intellect (Uttara Kalamrita sl. 8-9).
by_area.career: Favour from government and superiors, good standing, profit in trade (BPHS 47.62-65); an elevated position (Phaladeepika 19.10); errands or embassies (Jataka Parijata 18.133). Punishment or displeasure from government when Mercury is with malefics or in a dusthana (BPHS 47.66-68); trouble from the trading class (Uttara Kalamrita sl. 8-9).
by_area.finance: Wealth through business, seniors, relatives and friends (BPHS 47.64; Jataka Parijata 18.133); dealing in gold (Jataka Parijata 18.133). Loss of wealth, land and cattle when Mercury is in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.67-68).
by_area.health: Good health when Mercury is strong (BPHS 47.64). Wind ailments (Jataka Parijata 18.133); wind, heat and phlegm disorders (Phaladeepika 19.24); urinary trouble when Mercury is with malefics; rheumatism and jaundice when in a dusthana (BPHS 47.66-68).
by_area.relationships: Happiness from wife and children (BPHS 47.64; Phaladeepika 19.10). Marriage is mentioned for Mercury in Aries, Gemini, Leo and Virgo (Raman, HPA pp. 264-265); loss of wife and children for Mercury in Scorpio (Raman).
by_area.family: Birth of children in the early part (BPHS 47.69); enmity with relatives when Mercury is with malefics (BPHS 47.66); loss of relations when Mercury is malefic (Uttara Kalamrita sl. 8-9).
by_area.spirituality: Worship of gods and great men, benefit from spiritual teachers (Phaladeepika 19.24); religious and charitable work for Mercury in Aries, Virgo and Sagittarius; recitation of scriptures for Gemini and Capricorn (Raman, HPA pp. 264-265).

strengtheners: Mercury exalted, in its own sign or a friendly sign (BPHS 47.62)
Mercury in the 5th, 9th or 11th (Santhanam's reading) or in a kendra, the 11th or a trikona (Sanskrit gloss) (BPHS 47.62)
aspect of a benefic, placement in the 9th, or Mercury ruling the 10th, which gives the good results in full (BPHS 47.65)
Mercury retrograde, or vargottama (Phaladeepika 20.14, 20.22)
Mercury in an upachaya house from the lagna (Jataka Parijata 18.14, 18.16)
weakeners_or_cancellations: association with a malefic (BPHS 47.66)
placement in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.67-68)
debilitation, an enemy's sign, or the 6th or 12th: a benefic then gives only untoward results (Phaladeepika 20.27)
combustion ('eclipsed' by the Sun): adverse results (Phaladeepika 20.14)
library_entry.phases: BPHS 47.69-70: the start brings wealth, progress in education, birth of children and happiness; the middle brings recognition from government; the last part is distressing. Phaladeepika 20.57: a combust or debilitated Mercury in an auspicious sign or navamsa gives its good effects in the later part. Frawley (p. 203): the opening sub-period of a benefic's dasa plants seeds rather than fruit, and is a good time to set goals.
library_entry.disagreements: BPHS 47.62: Santhanam lists the 11th, 5th or 9th as an alternative to good dignity, while the Sanskrit gloss requires good dignity and also a kendra, the 11th or a trikona. BPHS gives the end of the dasa as distressing; Phaladeepika and Jataka Parijata do not divide the period. Phaladeepika 19.10 is wholly favourable, while 19.24 adds wind, heat and phlegm diseases. Raman makes Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces bad signs for this dasa even though Pisces is only Mercury's debilitation sign and Cancer and Scorpio are not named by the classical dasa verses. Phaladeepika 20.14 treats retrogression as favourable; other sources here are silent.
library_entry.phrasing_guidance: Frame this as a long period for study, communication, trade and networks, whose tone depends on Mercury's dignity, house and associations. Mention the troubled version only when the chart shows the listed conditions, and keep health notes general (nerves, digestion), with no diagnosis. Present the BPHS start-middle-end pattern as a tendency, not a certainty.
